purpose: Reuse the existing KFB VFX donor and curated FX texture sources for later combat/world presentation without creating a second combat, physics or hit-detection owner.

sources.selectedHandoff: tools/KFB-ToolBox/_inbox/KFB Style References/VFX + KEYS + ASSETS - kfb-asset-handoff-animation-lab (9).json

donorFacts: Existing donor renders; it does not decide what was hit.
Existing donor uses one quad pool, four orientations (camera, ground, surface, velocity) and flipbooks for primary punctuation.
Existing donor already separates host physics/combat from presentation and emits optional shake/hitstop/cue/react events.
Existing donor already has muzzle, impact, electric, smoke, dirt, scorch, tracer, slash/flame-style atlas roles and predrawn hit/electric flipbooks.
handoffCompatibilityNote: The linked asset handoff was generated for Animation Lab with allowedKinds=model-3d. The FX PNGs are source-present but consumerKindAllowed=false for that consumer. This is not a rejection of the FX themselves; they require the existing/dedicated VFX consumer rather than Animation Lab.

proposedGuardrails: Reuse kfb-vfx.js before building another renderer.
VFX never decides hit, damage, knockback, access or world state.
Treat blood as a new current candidate direction, not as already accepted visual canon.
Preview candidate textures/effects in isolation before integrating them into Combat or World.
Prefer semantic recipes/triggers so Combat/World code does not hardcode texture filenames everywhere.
Do not route 2D FX PNGs through Animation Lab just because the handoff filename says animation-lab.
Keep first pink-donut Player Proof independent from VFX work.
firstFutureProofs: Ranged: one real weapon muzzle socket -> muzzle_01/02 style flash only.
Melee: one real sword swing -> slash_01 style sweep only.
Hit: one host-supplied hit point -> impact_white or big_hit flipbook.
Blood option: same hit event -> blood_impact flipbook behind a visual toggle/human gate.
World: one static fire/smoke emitter and one access.unlock ring/glow cue.
